title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion, KV-cache scheduling, continuous batching
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production INT8/FP8 inference on our runtime was spending significant time in repeated dequantize/quantize paths and memory copies, and showed contention in KV-cache hot paths during continuous batching. This PR implements a set of coordinated optimizations: 1) a fused dequant -> smoothquant -> matmul kernel for INT8/FP8 codepaths (CUDA + AVX2 fallbacks) that avoids an intermediate FP32 allocation, 2) a dequantization-fusion pass in the kernel launcher that selects fused kernels when model graph patterns match, 3) KV-cache scheduling changes to pin dequantized KV pages for warm cache entries and avoid redundant dequant ops, and 4) tweaks to the continuous batching logic so fused kernels are favored when batch sizes hit quant-friendly thresholds. Results: microbenchmarks show 1.6-2.3x throughput improvements and 20-45% token-latency reduction on Llama-family 13B-70B INT8/FP8 workloads depending on sequence length and batch mix. Changes are behind a feature flag (runtime.enable_quant_fusion) and guarded by model-compat checks to avoid regressions for models with non-standard layer norms or custom quant params. This PR includes unit tests, perf harness updates, and a Canary config tuned for quant fusion verification. Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag, run perf-canary for 48h on dedicated nodes, enable for beta customers, then flip on by default after 2 weeks if no regressions. Related: ENG-12034, ENG-12890. Notes: careful attention was paid to numerical parity vs FP32 baseline; small differences (~0.3-0.7% RMSE on logits) observed for extreme outliers and covered in regression tests. See release notes section for guidance to customers (recommend enabling on dev and validating prompt sets).
